artifacts.summary: 8-phase plan to delete the four core -hard skills and three -hard agents, perform entry-level manifest routing surgery, and drive 359 references across 60 files to zero.

memory_candidates.content: When a task is chartered as 'pure deletion with zero rewiring' of system files, the charter's own file ledger is a lower bound, not the scope. Measure the real surface first with a repo-wide census of every deleted basename, then partition hits into three classes: (1) executable gates that hard-require the path (lint/test scripts with hardcoded path arrays) -- these must be retargeted BEFORE deletion or the suite goes red and post-deletion failures become unattributable; (2) structurally coupled declarations (manifest routing blocks, index-entries load_when.agents[] arrays) -- these must land in the SAME atomic commit as the deletion, because cross-validating lints fail on either half alone; (3) prose/comment citations -- safely deferred to a post-deletion sweep. Also: a charter directive to remove a whole config block wholesale is often wrong when the block is shared -- check whether each entry actually names a deleted asset before removing siblings that name live ones.
